name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 13 points and Huffman is an incumbent with over $1 million cash on hand
Challenger Robin Littau shows no reported fundraising or outside spending
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98 percent
No public general-election polling, so the estimate rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: A D+13 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with no visible fundraising or outside support leave little room for doubt, and markets price the race as near-certain for Democrats.
model.watch: A surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending, or unexpected polling showing a much tighter race, would warrant revisiting the forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jared Huffman, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Northern California district that leans thirteen points Democratic. He enters the general election with more than one million dollars on hand, while Republican Robin Littau reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending. No public general-election polls are available, but prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 98 percent chance of holding the seat.

The structural advantages are decisive: a strong partisan lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge. Huffman has won this district comfortably in past cycles, and nothing in the current evidence points to a competitive race. The absence of polling is the main caveat, but every available signal indicates a comfortable Democratic victory in November.
